fact: Government notice of 3 November 2017 publishes the National e-Government Strategy and Roadmap in terms of section 5(5) of the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2002 (Act 25 of 2002).

Notice 343 of 7 April 2017 publishes the proposed National e-Strategy for comment under section 5(3) of the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2002 (Act 25 of 2002), and says Parliament approved that Act.

The ICT SMME Development Strategy, gazetted 10 November 2017, describes the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act as an existing Act whose objects are to enable and facilitate electronic communications and transactions.

The Department of Communications' ICT policy colloquium discussion document, published 13 April 2012, refers to the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act of 2002 as the existing basis for the Universal Service Agency, Universal Service Fund and e-rate.
